title: Retention Orchestrator: Terraform module to provision CloudTrail + tiered OpenSearch/S3 archive
creator: Avery Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module (logging-retention-orchestrator) that provisions CloudTrail delivery, an S3 archive with automated lifecycle tiers, an OpenSearch domain with ILM (Index Lifecycle Management) policies, and operational health checks. The module must support both greenfield and in-place upgrades of existing customers' logging stacks, be parameterizable for retention windows and storage tiers, integrate KMS for encryption, and expose CloudWatch alarms + a small Lambda validator for end-to-end delivery checks.
acceptance_criteria: Module can be instantiated with minimal required variables to provision: CloudTrail, S3 bucket with lifecycle to Infrequent Access -> Glacier -> Deep Archive, OpenSearch domain with ILM, KMS key, and necessary IAM roles.
Existing customers with an S3 bucket created by prior modules can upgrade in-place: migration plan script demonstrates zero-data-loss and retention policy application in staging.
CloudWatch metrics and alarms are created for delivery failures, s3:ObjectCreated anomalies, OpenSearch yellow/red status; alerts map to an SNS topic used by on-call flows.

A Lambda-based health-check runs daily in a customer account: it verifies CloudTrail delivery, checks S3 object timestamps, and validates an OpenSearch index rollover policy. Failure paths create findings in the logging dashboard.
Terraform module passes terratest e2e suite in CI (creates resources in a sandbox account and tears them down) within a PR pipeline.
Documentation pages (Confluence) and example usage (monorepo terraform root) provided with recommended variable values for small/medium/large customers.
implementation_notes: Prefer AWS native primitives where possible (CloudTrail -> S3 -> OpenSearch ingestion) to reduce maintenance; avoid embedding heavy custom indexing logic in the module.
OpenSearch: use warm/cold/ilm policies to roll indices and delete after retention. Provide a toggle to optionally ship raw logs only to S3 (for customers who want managed OpenSearch elsewhere).
Use a single customer-managed KMS key for bucket + domain encryption. Offer guidance for cross-account key usage for central logging.
IAM roles: create least-privilege roles for CloudTrail delivery and for the health-check Lambda to read bucket/list indices. Keep policy documents as template files in the module for ease of review.

Upgrade path: implement a 'migration' script in /modules/logging-retention-orchestrator/tools that can run in safe mode (plan-only, then apply) and supports dry-run reporting. Document required timing for index rollover to avoid gaps.
State handling: encourage separate remote state for logging (dedicated S3 state and prefix). Provide a recommended lock table (DynamoDB) configuration.
Testing: terratest will run on a tiny instance type for OpenSearch; to reduce cost, we'll validate index creation/ilm application rather than full ingestion performance.

Make retention variables explicit: retention_days_open_search, s3_standard_days, s3_ia_days, s3_glacier_days, s3_deep_archive_days. Defaults follow legal+cost tradeoffs: 90/30/60/180/3650 as examples, but must be overridden per customer.
Expose opt-in cross-account delivery to central audit account (supports org-wide CloudTrail) with clear documentation and guardrails.
progress_updates: 2025-03-12: Ticket opened. Initial design doc sketched in Confluence (see links). Agreed module scope with PM: include health-check Lambda + CI tests.
2025-03-14: Prototype TF module skeleton created under github.com/redwood/terraform-modules/logging-retention-orchestrator. Basic CloudTrail + bucket + KMS provisioning passes local plan.
2025-03-16: Spike: evaluated two ILM strategies for OpenSearch (time-based vs size-based). Chose time-based rollover with optional size threshold to simplify customer expectations.
2025-03-18: Implemented S3 lifecycle rules for three-tier archive and added IAM role for CloudTrail delivery. Manual smoke test showed CloudTrail files arrive and lifecycle tags set.

2025-03-20: Added initial CloudWatch alarm definitions and a simple health-check Lambda (Python) that validates last object arrival and queries the OpenSearch _cat/indices API. Preparing PR for review.
review_feedback: Infra review (Rajiv Patel): tighten IAM on Lambda role; avoid s3:ListBucket for broad prefixes, scope by bucket+prefix. Also prefer kms:Decrypt vs * where possible.
Security (Maya Lopez): require default KMS key rotation enabled and include CMK alias naming convention. Add S3 bucket policies to block public access and force SSL.
Product (Lena Ortiz): add configuration knobs for 'compliance_mode' that enforces minimum retention windows and prevents accidental reduction in a release.
Design (Ops team): asked for a minimal dashboard template for the Console to visualize retention usage and incoming CloudTrail throughput. Created stub in related_links.
testing_plan: Unit tests: terragrunt + tflint static checks in pre-commit. Validate module variables and outputs contract.

Integration (CI): terratest that provisions module in sandbox account, pushes a sample CloudTrail event, asserts S3 object presence, verifies ILM rule creation on OpenSearch, and runs the Lambda health-check.
Upgrade test: create legacy bucket with prior lifecycle tags and run migration script in staging to validate no data movement loss and expected ILM assignment.
Chaos test (optional): simulate CloudTrail delivery failures (deny PutObject) to ensure alarms fire and health-check surfaces an error, and alerting path creates PagerDuty incident in staging.
rollout_plan: Merge PR to main after infra and security reviews are approved.
Publish module to internal Terraform registry with v0.1.0 and announce in #infra-alerts.
Run staged rollout: first deploy to 2 sandbox customer accounts, monitor for 72h for alarms or ILM surprises, then enable for 10 pilot customers, then general availability.
For customers on older modules: run the migration script per customer during a scheduled maintenance window (document recommended 1-3 hour window per account depending on index sizes).
Center the upgrade on safe default variables: do not shorten retention during migration by default and require explicit approval to decrease retention windows.
infra_changes: Add DynamoDB lock table recommendation to common infra module
Add a small Lambda (health-check) and its CloudWatch schedule resource
Create SNS topic for delivery failure alerts and default subscription to on-call via PagerDuty integration
